note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent judge, authored neither the annotation nor the tests) after the row gained {partial}. RFC 4301 Section 5.2 step 4, read in rfc/full/rfc4301.txt: "Apply AH or ESP processing as specified, using the SAD entry selected in step 3a above.  Then match the packet against the inbound selectors identified by the SAD entry to verify that the received packet is appropriate for the SA via which it was received." Tested: "match the packet against the inbound selectors identified by the SAD entry", for ESP the inbound XFRM state receives in its own form on the receiving interface. The tagged units are byte-identical to the previous judgement and still assert exact outcomes: TestRFC4301TransportModeInboundSADEntryDropsPacketsOutsideItsSelectors and TestRFC4301TunnelModeInboundSelectorsAreEnforcedByTheRequirePolicy deliver a decrypted packet inside the SA's selectors and drop one outside them on real XFRM (revert records on child.go::installChildSA and child.go::appendChildPolicies, both polarities); TestRFC4301TransportStateSelectorIsTheNegotiatedPair pins the transport state selector to the negotiated pair (mutant on child.go::inboundStateSelector); the boundary pair pins direction, selector and template of the inbound policy and refuses a widened port (mutants on xfrm_linux.go::xfrmPolicyFromParams and xfrmSelectorPort). Gap: "verify that the received packet is appropriate for the SA via which it was received". The split is by case, not by clause, and the reason says so: confirmed at the producer, internal/component/ike/dataplane/espform_linux.go::espFormReceiver.run reads bare ESP whose SPI is watched (a Child SA whose inbound state carries the ESP-in-UDP template, installed with UDPEncap on port 4500 with no NAT) and rawESPFormInjector.inject sends it to Ze's own address, so after decapsulation the packet arrives on lo, whose disable_policy=1 sets IPSKB_NOPOLICY and skips the inbound policy check; the decrypted packet is delivered whatever its inner addresses, which is also an unmet step 5 discard. The comment above espFormBypassInboundPolicy states the same defect. No tagged unit exercises that path, so the tags prove only the Tested case. Defect owned by plan/release/fixes/spec-ipsec-dual-form-receive-spd-bypass.md (journal plan/journal/escape-hatch-scoped-wider-than-its-justification.md 2026-11-10). The previous verdict, enforced, is withdrawn: it credited the whole requirement while a reachable inbound path delivers ESP-protected traffic with no selector check. Zero whole-requirement credit.
